title: Credential Broker: per-scope TTL, naming conventions, and emergency revoke workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We will implement an internal Credential Broker service to centralize lifecycle management for API keys and scoped tokens. The Broker provides per-scope TTL enforcement, canonical naming, a rotation operator, and an emergency revoke path that ties into audit logs and RBAC v2. This ticket covers design, prototype operator, e2e tests, migration scripts for existing tokens, and a documentation & rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Broker service deployed with feature flag
Per-scope TTL enforced for at least three token types (service, env, user-scoped)
Automatic naming rules applied on minting and renaming during migration
Rotation operator runs as k8s controller and completes a rolling rotation with zero downtime in staging
Emergency revoke API documented and exercised via drill; revocations appear in audit logs within 5s
Migration script migrates 95% of legacy tokens to scoped tokens without service disruptions
E2E tests covering happy path, rotation rollback, and audit enrichment
tasks: Design data model and naming schema for tokens
Build Credential Broker HTTP API and internal DB schema
Implement per-scope TTL enforcement and expiry sweeper
Create k8s operator for scheduled rotations and on-demand rotate endpoint
Add audit log hooks and ensure entries include actor, scope, prev_key_hash
Write migration script for legacy tokens and a dry-run mode
Add new RBAC v2 roles for token mint/revoke/rotate
Update Console UI to show token metadata and rotation status
Write runbook and incident playbook for emergency revoke
comments: 2025-11-10 - Aisha: Kickoff meeting with Security and Platform. Agreed to prototype on staging k8s cluster and prefer Postgres for broker metadata.
2025-11-17 - Diego: PoC of naming schema complete. Using pattern: <org>-<env>-<purpose>-YYYYMMDD-XXXX; added collision avoidance via sequence id.
2025-11-24 - Security review: requested stronger HSM integration for root key ops; flagged privacy for migration logs.
2025-11-28 - Diego: Built migration dry-run; found 120 legacy tokens lacking owner metadata. Created fallback mapping and follow-up task ENG-62400.
2025-12-02 - Aisha: Load test of rotation operator at 1k rotations/hour passed; measured audit log lag ~3.2s.
design_decisions: Use broker as single source of truth rather than in-place per-service rotation to centralize policy and auditing
Store non-sensitive metadata in Postgres; secrets remain in KMS and ephemeral caches
Operator will perform warm-swap rotations to avoid issuing two simultaneous valid keys for same scope
Name patterns are canonical and immutable except via approved migration jobs logged in audit
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy Broker behind feature flag in staging; 2) Enable per-scope TTL for non-critical service tokens; 3) Run migration dry-runs and reconcile owners; 4) Gradually enable for higher-impact token types and Dedicated customers; 5) Run org-wide emergency revoke drills and finalize runbooks.
risks: Migration exposes ownerless tokens requiring manual ownership resolution
Initial broker becomes single point of failure for mint/revoke—mitigated by caching and read-through fallbacks
Audit pipeline latency might temporarily exceed SLA during high rotation bursts
notes: Prefer KMS/HSM for signing and root key rotation; Vault integration already scoped in ENG-59800
Follow-on ticket suggested for Console UX polish: DES-220 (design)
audit_requirements: Every mint/rotate/revoke must emit an audit record with timestamp, actor_id, scope_id, previous_key_hash, rotation_id
Audit records must be indexed and searchable by scope_id and actor_id within 24 hours
Retention policy: 1 year for full audit records, 7 years for critical customer tokens
